parts.title: Part I – Multiple Choice Questions
parts.instructions: PART-I Contains 75 multiple-choice questions. You must answer all of them. Each question carries 1 point. Write all the answers on the SCANTRON GENERAL PURPOSE ANSWER SHEETS. There is only one best answer for each question.

parts.title: Part II – Workout and Short Answer Questions
parts.instructions: This part contains 8 questions. You must answer all of them. Each question carries 5 to 1 point as per its difficulty. A total of 25 points. Write your answers on separate answer sheet provided.

questions.answer: Limiting reactant Cl₂ (2 mol); excess H₂ (1 mol left). Yield: 4 mol HCl = 146 g = 89.6 L at STP.
accepted_answers: Limiting reactant Cl₂ (2 mol); excess H₂ (1 mol left). Yield: 4 mol HCl = 146 g = 89.6 L at STP.
explanation_steps: Given: 6 g H₂ = 3 mol; 142 g Cl₂ = 2 mol
Answer: limiting Cl₂; 4 mol; 146 g; 89.6 L
tips: Convert to moles before comparing.

questions.stem: Write any three differences between nuclear fission and nuclear fusion. (3 pts)
questions.answer: Fission: a heavy nucleus splits, used in reactors, products radioactive. Fusion: light nuclei join, powers the Sun, needs very high T, products usually lighter/less long-lived waste.
accepted_answers: Fission: a heavy nucleus splits, used in reactors, products radioactive. Fusion: light nuclei join, powers the Sun, needs very high T, products usually lighter/less long-lived waste.
explanation_steps: Fission splits heavy nuclei; fusion joins light nuclei
marking_points: 1 each for any three valid contrasts (split vs join; fuel; energy per nucleon; conditions; waste)
tips: Sun = fusion. Power station = fission.

questions.stem: CuCl₂(aq) + Al(s) → AlCl₃(aq) + Cu(s). Assign oxidation numbers and name the oxidized species, reducing agent, reduced species and oxidizing agent. (5 pts)

accepted_answers: Cu +2→0 (reduced; CuCl₂ oxidizing agent). Al 0→+3 (oxidized; Al reducing agent). Cl stays −1.
explanation_steps: Answer: Al oxidized / reducing agent; Cu²⁺ reduced / oxidizing agent
marking_points: 1 ox. numbers; 1 oxidized; 1 reducing agent; 1 reduced; 1 oxidizing agent
tips: The metal that goes into solution is oxidized.

questions.stem: Which of the underlined properties in the following paragraph are physical properties? Iodine is a grayish-black solid, which has a metallic luster and a characteristic odour. Its density is 4.93 g/cm³. When it is slowly heated it forms a purple vapour but it does not burn in the presence of oxygen. It is soluble in alcohol but not soluble in water. Iodine is poisonous and has a melting point of 113.5°C. (2 pts)
questions.answer: Physical: colour, luster, odour, density, purple vapour (sublimation), solubility, melting point. Chemical: does not burn; poisonous is a physiological effect.
accepted_answers: Physical: colour, luster, odour, density, purple vapour (sublimation), solubility, melting point. Chemical: does not burn; poisonous is a physiological effect.
explanation_steps: Physical = appearance, density, solubility, MP, sublimation
Answer: colour, luster, odour, density, vapour, solubility, MP
marking_points: 0.25 each for any eight physical items; 0.5 if combustion correctly excluded
tips: Physical: no new substance. Chemical: new substance / reactivity.
